observations.explanation: The paper describes a standalone environment that avoids live websites and imports real-world data into functional applications (PDF pp. 3–4). It also supports multiple observation formats and different element-selection methods (PDF pp. 4–5).
Evaluation covers textual answers as well as programmatic checks of intermediate states and task outcomes (PDF pp. 7–8).

The paper reports baseline success rates and analyzes failure modes, including mistaken infeasibility judgments and observation errors (PDF pp. 9–10). The low rate supports the benchmark’s difficulty, not a claim of progress. There is a small inconsistency: Table 3 reports 10.59%, while the prose says 10.63% (PDF p. 9).

The evaluated agents are text-based GPT-3.5/GPT-4 baselines, with a 30-transition limit; the paper identifies image-based observations and pixel-based actions as future work (PDF p. 9). Thus these results do not establish performance across other architectures or modalities.
